text: If I had more time, I'd learn to play the harp.
tip: 'I'd' is a short /aɪd/. Stress TIME and HARP. Pause a little at the comma.

text: I've been living here for nearly three years.
tip: 'I've been' squeezes into /aɪv bɪn/ because 'been' is weak. Stress LIV-ing, NEAR-ly and THREE.

text: The bridge was built by the villagers a hundred years ago.
tip: 'was' is weak /wəz/. 'built' rhymes with 'kilt' because the 'u' is silent.

text: She asked me whether I'd ever been to Scotland.
tip: 'asked' is /ɑːskt/, which is tricky! In fast speech many people say /ɑːst/. Stress SCOT-land.

text: You should have told me you were coming.
tip: 'should have' sounds like /ˈʃʊdəv/. Never write 'should of'!

text: Although it was raining, we decided to go for a walk.
tip: 'decided' has /ɪd/: de-CI-ded. Pause briefly after 'raining'.

text: I'm used to getting up early because of my job.
tip: 'used to' has an /s/, not a /z/: /ˈjuːstə/. Link 'getting up' into 'gettin-gup'.

text: The museum, which is in the city centre, is free on Sundays.
tip: Pause at both commas because the 'which' clause is extra information. Stress mu-SE-um.

text: I'm thinking of applying for a job at the bookshop.
tip: ap-PLY-ing has the stress in the middle. Link 'thinking of' into 'thinkin-gof'.

text: We'd better hurry, or we'll miss the last train.
tip: Keep the end sound: 'we'd' /wiːd/ and 'we'll' /wiːl/ must sound different.

text: Have you ever tried the cheese they make in this valley?
tip: Yes/no questions usually rise at the end. Keep /tr/ together in 'tried' /traɪd/.

text: It's the most interesting story I've ever read.
tip: 'interesting' often has three syllables: /ˈɪntrəstɪŋ/. Here 'read' is past, so say /red/.

text: Unless the weather improves, the festival will be cancelled.
tip: 'improves' ends in /vz/. 'cancelled' is /ˈkænsld/ with two syllables.

text: I'd rather stay at home than go to the crowded market.
tip: 'rather' and 'than' both have a buzzy /ð/. 'crowded' ends in /ɪd/.

text: The owl, who had been asleep all day, suddenly opened its eyes.
tip: Say it in three chunks: The owl | who had been asleep all day | suddenly opened its eyes.

text: Could you tell me what time the next boat leaves?
tip: Indirect questions often fall at the end. In 'next boat', say just one /t/: /neks bəʊt/.

text: My grandmother used to tell us stories about the old castle.
tip: Stress GRAND-mother, STOR-ies and CAS-tle. 'used to' is /ˈjuːstə/.

text: Neither my brother nor I could find the way home.
tip: British 'neither' is usually /ˈnaɪðə/. Stress BROTH-er and I.

q: Describe your perfect weekend. Use 'would' and 'because'.
model: My perfect weekend would start with a long walk because I love being outside.
tip: Make it one smooth sentence. 'would' is often weak /wəd/, or you can say 'it'd'.

q: Tell me about something you have never done. Start with 'I've never…'.
model: I've never been to Japan, but I would love to go one day.
tip: 'I've never' links into /aɪv ˈnevə/. Stress NEV-er and the place.

q: Give some advice to a friend who always feels tired. Use 'should'.
model: You should go to bed earlier and drink more water during the day.
tip: 'should' is weak /ʃəd/. Stress the advice itself: BED, EAR-li-er, WA-ter.

q: What will you do if it rains tomorrow? Begin with 'If it rains'.
model: If it rains tomorrow, I'll stay at home and read a good book.
tip: 'I'll' counts as 'I will'. Pause after the 'if' part and stress the main verb.

text: If I had a robot, it would tidy my room.
tip: 'would' is weak /wəd/. Stress RO-bot and TI-dy.

text: I've been learning the guitar for two years.
tip: 'I've been' sounds like /aɪv bɪn/. Stress gui-TAR and YEARS.

text: The festival was cancelled because of the storm.
tip: 'cancelled' ends with /ld/: /ˈkænsld/. Stress FES-ti-val and STORM.

text: Although it was raining, we enjoyed the picnic.
tip: Pause a little after 'raining,'. Stress al-THOUGH /ɔːlˈðəʊ/ and en-JOYED.

text: You'd better wear a helmet when you ride your bike.
tip: 'You'd better' links into /juːd ˈbetə/. Stress HEL-met.

text: My cousin, who lives in Canada, is visiting us.
tip: Pause at each comma, and let your voice drop a little on 'who lives in Canada'.

text: We should recycle more plastic at school.
tip: Stress re-CY-cle and PLAS-tic. 'should' is weak /ʃəd/.

text: The volcano hasn't erupted for hundreds of years.
tip: 'hasn't' is one beat with a /z/: /ˈhæznt/. Stress vol-CA-no and e-RUP-ted.

text: I'm not sure, but I think the shop closes at six.
tip: Slow down on 'I'm not sure' and stress SURE. 'closes' has two buzzy /z/ sounds: /ˈkləʊzɪz/.

q: What is your favourite season and why? Use 'because'.
model: My favourite season is autumn because I love jumping in the leaves.
tip: 'because' is weak /bɪkəz/, so stress the reason itself: AU-tumn, LEAVES.

q: Describe your best friend. Use 'kind' or 'funny'.
model: My best friend is really funny and she always helps me with maths.
tip: Stress the describing word: really FUN-ny. Link 'helps me' smoothly.

q: What did you do last weekend? Use 'and then'.
model: On Saturday I played football, and then I went to the cinema with my dad.
tip: Make the -ed in 'played' a soft /d/. Pause a little before 'and then'.

q: What would you like to be when you grow up? Start with 'I'd like to be'.
model: I'd like to be a vet because I love animals.
tip: 'I'd like' links into /aɪd laɪk/. Stress VET and AN-i-mals.

q: Compare cats and dogs. Use 'than'.
model: Dogs are more playful than cats, but cats are easier to look after.
tip: 'than' is weak /ðən/. Stress the describing words: PLAY-ful, EAS-i-er.

q: Invite a friend to do something this weekend. Use 'Would you like to'.
model: Would you like to come swimming with me on Saturday afternoon?
tip: 'Would you' links into /wʊdʒu/. Let your voice go up at the end of the question.

q: Tell me about a time you were surprised. Use 'when'.
model: I was really surprised when my grandma came to my birthday party from Spain.
tip: Stress sur-PRISED and GRAND-ma. Slow down for the exciting part.

q: What do you do to stay healthy? Use 'usually' or 'often'.
model: I usually walk to school and I often eat fruit after lunch.
tip: Put 'usually' before the verb. Stress U-su-al-ly and FRUIT.

q: Should children have homework? Start with 'I think'.
model: I think children should have a little homework, but not every day.
tip: Say 'I think' lightly, then stress the important words: LIT-tle, NOT, EV-ery DAY.

text: If it doesn't rain tomorrow, we'll go camping by the lake.
tip: Pause at the comma. 'we'll' is one beat /wiːl/. Stress CAMP-ing and LAKE.

text: The new playground was opened by a famous footballer.
tip: 'was' is weak /wəz/. 'opened' is two syllables: /ˈəʊpənd/.

text: I've already finished my project, but Tom hasn't started yet.
tip: Stress the contrast: al-READ-y and YET. 'finished' ends in /ʃt/.

text: She's the girl whose dog won the prize at the show.
tip: 'whose' sounds like 'who's' /huːz/. Stress DOG and PRIZE.

text: We were walking home when we saw a shooting star.
tip: 'were' is weak /wə/. Stress WALK-ing, SHOOT-ing STAR.

text: Could you remind me what our science homework is?
tip: In indirect questions the verb comes last: 'what our homework IS'. Voice goes up a little at the end.

text: I'm looking forward to seeing my cousins in the summer.
tip: 'forward to' links into /ˈfɔːwəd tə/. Stress SEE-ing and COUS-ins.

text: The robot competition is going to be held in our school hall.
tip: Stress com-pe-TI-tion and RO-bot. 'going to be' is quick and light.

text: It must be cold outside, because everyone is wearing scarves.
tip: 'must be' links into /məsbi/. 'scarves' ends with /vz/.

text: As soon as the bell rang, the children rushed outside.
tip: Pause after 'rang,'. 'rushed' is one syllable ending in /ʃt/.

q: Tell me about a book you enjoyed. Start with 'The book is about'.
model: The book is about a girl who finds a dragon egg, and I loved the ending.
tip: Stress the key words: GIRL, DRAG-on EGG. 'who finds' links smoothly.

q: Describe your school. Use 'there is' or 'there are'.
model: There are about five hundred students in my school, and there is a big vegetable garden.
tip: 'there are' is quick /ðər ɑː/. Stress HUN-dred and VEG-e-ta-ble.

q: What would you do if you found a lost puppy? Start with 'If I found'.
model: If I found a lost puppy, I would check its collar and call the number on it.
tip: Pause after 'puppy,'. 'I would' can be 'I'd' /aɪd/. Stress COL-lar and NUM-ber.

q: Give a friend advice about learning to swim. Use 'You should'.
model: You should start in the shallow end and practise kicking with a float.
tip: 'should' is weak /ʃəd/. Stress SHAL-low and FLOAT.

q: What have you learned this year? Use 'I've learned' or 'I've learnt'.
model: This year I've learned how to make pancakes, and I've learnt three French songs.
tip: 'I've' is one beat /aɪv/. Stress PAN-cakes and FRENCH SONGS.

q: Describe a place you would like to visit. Use 'would like to'.
model: I would like to visit Japan because I want to see the cherry blossom.
tip: 'I'd like to' is fine too: /aɪd laɪk tə/. Stress ja-PAN and BLOS-som.

q: What did you do on your last birthday? Use 'first' and 'after that'.
model: First I opened my presents with my family, and after that we went bowling with my friends.
tip: Pause a little after 'First' and before 'after that'. 'opened' is two syllables.

q: How do you help at home? Use 'sometimes' or 'every day'.
model: I sometimes wash the dishes, and every day I feed our cat before school.
tip: Put 'sometimes' before the verb. Stress DISH-es and FEED.

q: Tell me about a small problem you solved. Use 'so'.
model: I forgot my lunch box last week, so my friend shared her sandwiches with me.
tip: Pause a little before 'so', then stress the result: SHARED, SAND-wich-es.

q: Which is better, the beach or the mountains? Use 'I prefer'.
model: I prefer the mountains because I love hiking and the air feels fresher there.
tip: Stress pre-FER on the second part. Stress MOUN-tains and FRESH-er.
